claims.text: The initial material is an additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with a dual-nanoprecipitation microstructure.
High-temperature oxidation causes significant elemental redistribution within or around the nanoprecipitates.
The nanoprecipitates act as sites for elemental segregation.
The nanoprecipitates or their interfaces act as sites for oxide formation.
High-temperature oxidation drives oxidation-prone elements toward nanoprecipitate interfaces.
Cr and Ti are specifically expected to migrate toward and accumulate at nanoprecipitate interfaces.
Element-enriched zones at nanoprecipitate interfaces form thin protective oxide layers.
The proposed protective oxide layers mitigate further oxidation.
APT can capture atomic-scale compositional gradients associated with the proposed redistribution.
Post-oxidation APT will reveal a measurable elemental gradient at nanoprecipitate boundaries.
The boundary gradients will correlate with the development of thin protective oxide layers.
The proposed redistribution and oxide formation explain enhanced oxidation resistance.
The as-manufactured, non-oxidized baseline has no comparable elemental redistribution.
The proposed mechanism may be specific to additively manufactured HEAs with dual nanoprecipitation.
Changes in alloy composition or use of cast or wrought processing routes could produce different oxidation behavior.
